abstract: Patients who undergo chemotherapy for metastatic nonseminomatous germ cell cancer of the testis often undergo subsequent resection of residual tissue. We performed a retrospective review of 11 consecutive patients who had their resected residual tissue cultured in a soft agar clonogenic assay to determine if there were any biological data that could be obtained in this setting. Twelve assays were performed on the 11 patients. Some colony formation occurred in 10 of the 12 assays, including 4 of 5 assays in which cancer was found and 6 of 7 in which no cancer was found. The rate of colony formation, however, was significantly less for the noncancerous tissues than for the ones with cancer noted (p = 0.019). Three of the patients with cancer are dead, while all of those with benign tissue remain free of disease, with follow-up ranging from three to six years. Our data suggest that clonogenic growth from resected tissue after chemotherapy has the potential to supplement histologic findings, possibly as a predictor of the future biologic behavior of a patient's disease process.
abstract_ja: 転移性の精巣の非セミノーマ性胚細胞腫瘍に対して化学療法を受けた患者は、その後、残存組織の切除を受けることが多い。我々は、軟寒天を用いたクローン原性アッセイで切除された残存組織を培養した11例の連続症例を後方視的に検討し、組織の生物学的データが得られるかどうかを調べた。11例で12回のアッセイを行った。12件中10件でコロニー形成がみられ、そのうちがんが認められた5件中4件、がんが認められなかった7件中6件で形成された。コロニー形成の割合は、がんが認められた組織の方が非がん組織よりも有意に高かった（p=0.019）。がんを認めた患者のうち3名は死亡しているが、良性組織の患者は追跡期間3〜6年で無病である。化学療法後の切除組織からのクローン原性増殖は、組織学的所見を補完し、疾患の将来の生物学的挙動を予測する因子となる可能性がある。
